root.meaning: a jacket worn under other clothes

history: The jupe was first worn by men, and on top. Arabic ǧubba was a kind of jacket worn under other clothes. The word travelled to southern Italy, where jupa is recorded in 1053 for a garment of eastern origin, and to Genoa, where Latin documents have juppum in 1165. In French, around 1188, a jupe is a padded doublet fitted to a man's chest, and a little earlier a text already puts one on a woman. The meaning ‘skirt’ only appears in 1603; the jupe then replaced the older word cotillon. Italian giubba kept the upper half of the story. In shops you will find la jupe droite, ‘the straight skirt’, and la mini-jupe.
historyEinfach: Jupe comes from an Arabic word for a jacket. It came to French through Italian. In the Middle Ages, a jupe was a short jacket for men. Only in 1603 did it start to mean a skirt for women. Italian giubba is still a jacket.

elsewhere.text: Italian took the same Arabic word. There it stayed a garment for the upper body, while in French it moved down to become a skirt.
